t.6.75.1: Hearing the words of Vibhīṣaṇa, Rāvaṇi, overwhelmed with rage, spoke harsh words and sprang forward with great speed.
t.6.75.2: With weapons and sword uplifted, he stood upon a great, well-adorned chariot yoked with black horses, resembling Kāla, the Ender, himself.
t.6.75.3: Raising his terrible bow, huge in size, broad, swift and sturdy, and grasping his arrows that destroy enemies...
t.6.75.4: Roused to fury, he spoke to Saumitri, together with Vibhīṣaṇa, and to those tigers among the monkeys: "Behold my prowess!"
t.6.75.5: Today in battle, will you be able to ward off the irresistible shower of arrows loosed from my bow, like rain released from the sky?
t.6.75.6: Today my arrows, loosed from my mighty bow, will scatter and destroy your limbs, as fire consumes a heap of cotton.
t.6.75.7: Today I shall send every one of you to the abode of Yama, pierced through by sharp arrows and by spears, darts, swords and lances.
t.6.75.8: When I, swift of hand, loose showers of arrows in battle, roaring like a thundercloud, who will stand before me?
t.6.75.9: Hearing that roar of the lord of the rākṣasas, Lakṣmaṇa then, enraged yet with a fearless face, spoke these words to Rāvaṇi.
t.6.75.10: You have declared, O Rākṣasa, that the far shore of undertakings is hard to reach; but he who reaches the far shore of his undertakings through action is truly wise.
t.6.75.12: The course you followed then in battle, when you had made yourself invisible, is a path trodden by thieves; it is not one practised by heroes.
t.6.75.11: You, who have fallen short of a goal that is hard for anyone to attain, merely by uttering words imagine, 'I have achieved my purpose,' O evil-minded one!
t.6.75.13: O Rākṣasa, I stand here, having come within the range of your arrows. Show me that might of yours today; why do you boast with mere words?
t.6.75.14: Thus addressed, the mighty Indrajit, victorious in battle, seized his fearsome bow and released sharpened arrows.
t.6.75.15: Those arrows, discharged with great force and like serpent's venom, reached Lakṣmaṇa and fell upon him like hissing snakes.
t.6.75.16: In battle the swift Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa, pierced Saumitri, who bore auspicious marks, with arrows of exceedingly great speed.
t.6.75.17: His limbs deeply pierced by arrows and drenched with blood, the glorious Lakṣmaṇa shone like a smokeless fire.
t.6.75.18: But Indrajit, having surveyed and comprehended his own deed, let out a very great roar and spoke these words.
t.6.75.19: O Saumitri, today those feathered arrows with sharpened edges, loosed from my bow and bringing life to its end, will take away your life.
t.6.75.20: Today, O Lakṣmaṇa, let packs of jackals, flocks of hawks, and vultures swoop down upon you as you lie lifeless, slain by me.
t.6.75.21: Rāma, that degenerate kṣatriya, ever ignoble and utterly evil-minded, shall this very day behold you, his devoted brother, slain by me.
t.6.75.22: Today, O Saumitri, you shall be seen upon the ground, slain by me, your armor hacked to pieces, your bow flung aside, and your head struck off.
t.6.75.23: To the son of Rāvaṇa, who was enraged and speaking harshly in this way, Lakṣmaṇa replied with words that were exceedingly well-reasoned.
t.6.75.24: Why do you boast here, O Rākṣasa, without having performed the deed? Perform that deed by which I may believe your boasting.
t.6.75.25: Without uttering a single harsh word, without insulting you in the least, and without boasting, I shall slay you; watch, O man-eater!
t.6.75.26: Having spoken thus, Lakṣmaṇa drove into the rākṣasa's chest five iron arrows of tremendous speed, shafts drawn back to the ear.
t.6.75.27: Struck by him with arrows, the son of Rāvaṇa, filled with rage, pierced Lakṣmaṇa in return with three well-aimed shafts.
t.6.75.28: There arose in battle a tumultuous and most terrible clash between those two lions among men and rākṣasas, each seeking to slay the other.
t.6.75.29: For both were endowed with strength, both were rich in valour; both were exceedingly bold in their onset, and both were skilled in all weapons and missiles.
t.6.75.30: Both great heroes, supremely hard to conquer and of matchless strength and splendor, fought each other like two planets that have entered the sky.
t.6.75.31: Like Bala and Vṛtra, those two great-souled warriors, truly hard to assail in battle, then fought each other like two lions.
t.6.75.32: Standing firm and releasing many floods of arrows, those two lions among men and rākṣasas, thrilled with joy, fought against each other.
t.6.75.33: Those two foremost of men and rākṣasas, greatly thrilled, eager for victory and bearing arrows and bows, rained down upon each other fiercely with a shower of streams of arrows, like two rain-clouds.
